body:
## Pull request overview

This PR tightens view configuration handling to align with the `@objectstack/spec` nested config format by removing flat-property fallbacks, adding dev-time migration warnings, and updating console fixtures/tests to the nested structure.

**Changes:**
- Removed flat view-config fallbacks in console and `plugin-view` `ObjectView` implementations so only nested type-specific config is used.
- Added development-mode `console.warn` to surface flat-property usage and guide migrations.
- Updated console test fixtures and added a new test validating flat keys are ignored.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx | Enforces nested-only access for type-specific view options and adds a dev warning when flat keys are detected. |
| apps/console/src/components/ObjectView.tsx | Removes flat fallbacks for view-specific options and adds a dev warning; refactors chart config reads to `viewDef.chart`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ViewSwitching.test.tsx | Updates mock object metadata to use `listViews` and nested view configs. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/SpecViewConfig.test.tsx | New test ensuring flat view config keys are ignored and defaults are used. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ObjectView.test.tsx | Updates fixtures to use `listViews` and nested view configs. |
</details>

`ObjectChart` receives `schema.filter` and uses it directly as `$filter` when querying. This change now sources `filter` from `viewDef.chart.filter`, but in the rest of the view model (and examples) `filter` is a top-level view property (e.g., listViews.active.filter). If a chart view sets `filter` at the view root, it will now be ignored. Keep `filter` as `viewDef.filter` (generic view-level config), while still enforcing nested-only access for chart-specific keys (chartType/xAxisField/etc.).
```suggestion
                        filter: viewDef.filter,
```

For calendar/gantt, `titleField` now defaults to `'name'` even when the object’s configured title field is something else (e.g., events often use `subject`). Since `objectDef.titleField` is already used as the default for kanban/timeline/map/gallery, consider using it here too (`viewDef.<type>?.titleField || objectDef.titleField || 'name'`). This keeps spec enforcement (nested-only) while avoiding regressions on objects that don't have a `name` field.

The warning message says to migrate flat keys under `options.${viewType}`, but in this code path `viewOptions` can be the active view object itself (not its `.options`), and the nested spec shape is typically `${viewType}.{...}`. Consider adjusting the message to reflect the actual expected nesting for the input shape being checked, otherwise the guidance is misleading during migrations.
```suggestion
                `Move them under the "${viewType}" nested config object per @objectstack/spec protocol.`
```

`generateViewSchema` now ignores flat properties (and warns in dev) to enforce nested config, but there are currently no tests in `packages/plugin-view` asserting that behavior for each view type (kanban/calendar/timeline/etc.). Adding a focused unit test that verifies flat keys are ignored and nested keys are honored would help prevent regressions when this logic changes again.

In `options.kanban`, `cardFields` is always set but can be `undefined` when the view doesn't define `viewDef.kanban.columns`. Because ListView later spreads `schema.options.kanban` over its own defaults, an explicit `cardFields: undefined` will override the default (`schema.fields`) and can break kanban rendering. Omit `cardFields` entirely unless it's defined (or strip `undefined` keys from the options object before passing it).
```suggestion
                    ...(viewDef.kanban?.columns ? { cardFields: viewDef.kanban.columns } : {}),
```

Several option blocks set properties that may be `undefined` (e.g., `calendar.endDateField`, `map.locationField`, `gantt.progressField/dependenciesField`). Since ListView composes the final child schema as `{ defaults..., ...(schema.options.<type> || {}) }`, passing an explicit `undefined` will overwrite the default and remove it. Consider only including these keys when defined (or normalize options by removing `undefined` values) so ListView defaults like `'end_date'`, `'location'`, `'progress'`, etc. still apply.
